item.title: David Njoku announces he won’t re-sign with Browns
item.description: This was not nearly as dramatic as former Cavaliers star LeBron James announcing to a national audience on ESPN that he was taking his talents to South Beach in the summer of 2010. But one day after the Super Bowl, David Njoku announced he’ll be taking his talents — somewhere else. After nine seasons playing tight end for the Browns, Njoku announced in an Instagram post that he’ll use free agency to find a different team when it begins next month. item.description: All-Star weekend is back in California for the second straight year, this time moving to Inglewood for the NBA’s annual midseason showcase. Among the on-court events are the celebrity game and Rising Stars competition on Feb. 13, 3-point, Shooting Stars and slam-dunk contests on Feb. 14 and a new All-Star game format on Feb. 15 that features the USA vs. the World. item.title: Donovan Mitchell, James Harden rally Cavaliers to 119-117 win over Nuggets
item.description: By MICHAEL KELLY DENVER — Donovan Mitchell scored 32 points, including two free throws with 0.9 seconds left after James Harden’s tying 3-pointer, and the Cavaliers rallied to beat the Nuggets 119-117 on Feb. 10. Harden finished with 22 points and 10 rebounds in his second game with Cleveland. Harden, acquired from the Los Angeles Clippers on Feb. 4, scored 23 points in his Cavaliers debut three nights later.
